note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in IN.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Ohio River Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 56, SR 156, SR 62, SR 66 and local roads along the Ohio River, Ohio line near Lawrenceburg to the Illinois line west of Mount Vernon, 13 counties; SR 265 from the Kentucky line to SR 62 added 2018

facts.fact: The Indiana section is a 302-mile route across 13 southern Indiana counties, designated a state scenic byway in 1992 and a National Scenic Byway in 1996.
Indiana's segments, listed east to west, total 302.38 miles and end at SR 62 to the Illinois border.

Attractions on the byway include Devonian era fossil beds at the Falls of the Ohio, Angel Mounds State Historic Site at Evansville and historic New Harmony with buildings of its two communal societies.

byways.review: On June 25, 2018 the INDOT Commissioner added SR 265 from the Indiana-Kentucky border (Lewis and Clark Bridge) to SR 62 as a state scenic byway addition to this byway (order: https://www.in.gov/dA/632a724c74/6-25-18_SR265_ScenicByway_Comissioner_Order.pdf?language_id=1). Catalog maps 286.7 Indiana miles against the 302 the byway organization lists; check whether the SR 265 spur is drawn.

byways.name: Historic National Road
byways.designation: All-American Road (state byway 1996, National Scenic Byway 1998)
byways.where: Mostly US 40, Ohio line at Richmond to the Illinois line west of Terre Haute, 9 counties

facts.fact: The Indiana section is a 156-mile, nine-county corridor mostly signed as US 40, passing Terre Haute, Indianapolis and Richmond; views alternate between farm scenes and pike towns.
The Indiana National Road Association supported Plainfield's preservation and relocation of an original tollhouse and Richmond's preservation efforts in the Whitewater River Gorge.
Indiana's section was designated a state scenic byway in 1996, a National Scenic Byway in 1998, and part of the six-state All-American Road in 2002.
FHWA lists the Indiana National Road Association as the byway's Indiana contact.

byways.name: Indiana's Historic Pathways
byways.where: US 50 from Lawrenceburg to Vincennes and US 150 from Clarksville/New Albany to Vincennes, joined between Shoals and Vincennes

facts.fact: INDOT's 2004 designation letter describes the byway as essentially US 50 from Lawrenceburg to Vincennes and US 150 from Clarksville to Vincennes.

US 150 from Vincennes to New Albany is part of Indiana's Historic Pathways because it roughly parallels the Buffalo Trace; US 150 and US 50 run together from Vincennes to Shoals, paralleling the East Fork White River between Loogootee and Shoals, and US 150 passes Paoli's Courthouse Square.
FHWA describes a route first trodden by bison, later used by pioneers and stagecoaches, 250 miles long.

byways.review: No byway organization website found (the old support group's domains do not resolve); FHWA page used. INDOT says Clarksville, Wikipedia says New Albany for the US 150 end.

byways.name: Wabash River Scenic Byway
byways.where: Tippecanoe County: CR 875 West from Ross Hills County Park, Division Road, South River Road and North River Road (former SR 43) to I-65/SR 43

facts.fact: Designated as the River Road Scenic Byway in June 2008 and renamed the Wabash River Scenic Byway by Commissioner's order in 2016; the route runs from Ross Hills County Park on CR 875 West and Division Road to South River Road, then North River Road (former SR 43) to the I-65/SR 43 interchange.
The 2008 application maps show Fort Ouiatenon beside South River Road on the Wabash, and Tecumseh Trail parks and the proposed Prophetstown State Park entrance near the I-65 end.

byways.review: Catalog name is the pre-2016 'River Road Scenic Byway'. INDOT has no web page for it; the Commissioner's renaming order PDF is used as url.

byways.name: Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 38, SR 1, SR 121, US 52, old US 52 and US 50, Hagerstown (Wayne Co.) to Lawrenceburg (Dearborn Co.)

facts.fact: Designated in June 2008, the byway uses portions of SR 38, SR 1, SR 121, US 52, old US 52 and US 50 from Hagerstown in Wayne County to Lawrenceburg in Dearborn County.
The canal (1836 to 1847) ran 76 miles from Lawrenceburg to Hagerstown through Brookville, Metamora, Laurel, Connersville and Cambridge City.
At Metamora the canal still holds water, powering a restored grain mill, and crosses Duck Creek on a reconstruction of an 1846 wooden aqueduct, a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark.

byways.review: The byway's former website (whitewatercanalbyway.com) is now a parked domain; INDOT designation PDF used as url.

byways.name: Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway Loop Routes
byways.designation: State Scenic Byway (loop routes added to the Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway)
byways.where: East Fork Loop: US 40 to Richmond, US 27 to Liberty, SR 101 to Brookville. Oldenburg-Batesville Loop: SR 229 from Metamora to Batesville, SR 46 to St. Leon, SR 1 to US 52. Dearborn-Ripley Loop: US 50 Lawrenceburg to Aurora, SR 350 to Milan, SR 101 to Sunman, county roads to Dover, SR 1 back to Lawrenceburg

facts.fact: The three loops, the East Fork Loop, Oldenburg-Batesville Loop and Dearborn-Ripley Loop, were added to the Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway by Commissioner's order in September 2011.

The East Fork Loop runs east on US 40 to Richmond, south on US 27 to Liberty and SR 101 to Brookville; the Oldenburg-Batesville Loop takes SR 229 to Batesville and SR 46 to St. Leon; the Dearborn-Ripley Loop runs from Lawrenceburg to Aurora, Milan and Sunman.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. No agency GIS line exists; would need to be drawn from the order's road descriptions. Could alternatively be folded into the Whitewater Canal entry rather than shown separately.

byways.name: Historic Michigan Road Byway
byways.where: Madison to Michigan City: US 421 to Indianapolis, US 421 and SR 29 to Logansport, SR 25 to Rochester, old US 31 to South Bend, US 20 to Michigan City; 14 counties

facts.fact: Designated a state byway in 2011 from Madison to Michigan City; the road was commissioned by the Indiana General Assembly in the 1820s as the first state road and closely follows US 421, SR 29, SR 25, old US 31 and US 20.

The road passes through 14 counties and towns including Madison, Greensburg, Shelbyville, Indianapolis, Kirklin, Logansport, Rochester, Plymouth, South Bend and Michigan City, and is now a series of county, state and US highways.

byways.review: Catalog line covers only 33.6 miles (bbox lat 38.74 to 39.21, the US 421 stretch north of Madison toward Versailles/Napoleon); the designated byway runs the full length from Madison to Michigan City. Catalog line needs replacing.

byways.name: Lincoln Highway Scenic Byway
byways.designation: State Scenic Byway (Indiana Lincoln Highway Byway)
byways.where: 1913 route: Ohio line, Fort Wayne, Goshen, Elkhart, South Bend, La Porte, Valparaiso; 1928 route: Fort Wayne, Columbia City, Warsaw, Plymouth to Valparaiso; then US 30 corridor to the Illinois line at Dyer

facts.fact: Designated in 2011 using both the 1913 alignment (Fort Wayne, Goshen, Elkhart, South Bend, LaPorte, Valparaiso) and the 1928 alignment (Fort Wayne, Whitley, Kosciusko, Marshall and Starke counties), which meet at Valparaiso.
The 1928 route passes Columbia City, Warsaw and Plymouth.
The Lincoln Highway was conceived by Indianapolis entrepreneur Carl G. Fisher and first dedicated on October 31, 1913.

byways.name: Hoosier Hills State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 39 from Belleville (US 40) to Monrovia, SR 42 to Mooresville, SR 67, Blue Bluff Road to Martinsville, SR 252 to Morgantown, SR 135 through Nashville to US 50 west of Brownstown; Hendricks, Morgan, Brown and Jackson counties

facts.fact: The 83-mile route runs from Belleville at US 40 by SR 39, SR 42, SR 67 and Blue Bluff Road to Martinsville, then SR 252 to Morgantown and SR 135 through Bean Blossom, Nashville and Story to US 50 about three miles west of Brownstown.
It passes the courthouse squares of Martinsville (1859 Italianate courthouse) and Nashville (1873-74 Greek Revival courthouse) and runs along or through Brown County State Park.
Bean Blossom's Bill Monroe Park hosts what the application calls the longest continuously running bluegrass festival in the world.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. INDOT links only the September 2020 application, not a Commissioner's order; it appears as designated on INDOT's statewide map dated 9/16/2021. No agency GIS line; draw from the route description (part of the Hendricks County section is segmented).

issues: Historic Michigan Road catalog line (the-historic-michigan-road-byway-81469) is only 33.6 miles near Madison; the designated byway runs Madison to Michigan City through 14 counties.
Hoosier Hills: INDOT lists it as state-designated and shows it on the 2021 map, but the only linked document is the Sept 2020 application; no Commissioner's order was found.
Ohio River Scenic Byway: SR 265 (Kentucky line to SR 62, Clark County) was added in 2018; check whether the catalog line includes it (catalog IN miles 286.7 vs 302 listed by the byway organization).
INDOT's /dA/ PDF links on the program page 404 on secure.in.gov but work on www.in.gov; the www.in.gov form of the program page itself 404s. URLs in this file use the working www.in.gov PDF form.
FHWA's state selector says 'Indiana - 4' but its Indiana page shows only three byways (Ohio River, Historic Pathways, National Road).

Whitewater Canal Scenic Byway's own website (whitewatercanalbyway.com) is a parked domain; Hoosier Hills and Historic Pathways have no organization sites found (web search budget was exhausted, so a site may exist).
INDOT program page links ohioriverbyway.com and indiananationalroad.org over http; the National Road association now lives at https://indiananationalroad.com/.
Lincoln Highway catalog (287.8 mi) likely includes both alignments; not verified against the 1913/1928 split.
